title: Zugzwang

D0.outcome: Explains zugzwang: a position in which any move worsens the position of the player who must move.

D1.outcome: Told it is zugzwang, finds the key move and the spare tempo.

D2.outcome: In unlabeled king-and-pawn positions with locked pawns, predicts win, draw or loss for each side to move, including positions where a spare pawn move means the idea does not apply.

D3.outcome: Uses corresponding squares and a tempo-losing detour to change who is to move, and applies zugzwang to simple piece endings.

misconceptions: Every blocked position is a zugzwang.
The side with the move is always better.
sources: docs/curriculum-map-v1.1.md §3 (END.ZUGZWANG T3 D1 / T4 D3, merged)
conditions: Little room to manoeuvre, blocked pawns, no pieces whose moves could pass the turn.
A defender whose piece has only one job is the usual victim.
contrasts: A nearly identical placement where a spare pawn move exists, so the idea does not apply.
Calling any blocked position a zugzwang.
Open play where the kings simply race.

soft_prereq_notes.END.KPK.D1: K+P v K is where zugzwang is first felt
